title: Electric car: launch the design
target: Plan a safe team workflow and identify the car’s energy pathway.
criteria: Label the battery, switch, motor and connections.
Identify safety checkpoints before tools or power.
Connect a design choice with a measurable outcome.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A model delivery car has a charged battery, wires, a motor, and an open switch. Which part must change state to complete the intended path?
options: The switch must close.
The battery must be shorted.
The wires must be removed.
The motor must become a battery.
cpa.guide: Closing the switch completes the intended series path through the motor. A short bypasses the load and is unsafe.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A diagram labels the battery as the part that directly turns the axle. Which correction makes the diagram accurate?
options: The wires store all the car’s fuel.
The wheels create charge.
The switch creates the chemical energy.
The motor converts electrical input into axle rotation.
cpa.guide: The battery supplies energy; the motor produces rotation. The other parts do not create energy or charge.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A team wants to adjust a loose wire near a moving gear during a powered test. Which is the appropriate first step?
options: Hold the gear while the motor runs.
Increase voltage to move the wire away.
Stop and disconnect power before adjusting the wire.
Use a metal tool across the battery terminals.
cpa.guide: Disconnecting power prevents unexpected motion and short circuits during adjustment.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A student has a marked chassis but has not received the required tool checkpoint. What should happen before cutting?
options: Cut quickly before asking.
Get the teacher checkpoint and follow the tool’s safe-use procedure.
Have an untrained partner hold it by the blade.
Treat a sketch as permission to use any tool.
cpa.guide: A design drawing does not replace supervision and the required safety checkpoint.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A team predicts that removing wheel rubbing will improve straight travel. Which result would directly test that prediction?
options: Compare the paint colors.
Compare sideways drift over the same measured path before and after the adjustment.
Record only whether the motor makes noise.
Compare unrelated cars on different slopes.
cpa.guide: A controlled same-path comparison links the change to a measurable motion outcome.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: Two proposed cars differ only in wheel diameter. Which planning statement is testable?
options: Large wheels guarantee a win on any course.
Wheel size has no measurable effect.
At the same measured axle rate, the larger wheel should travel farther per second.
The larger wheel is always the best-looking design.
cpa.guide: Distance per turn is circumference. At fixed axle rate, larger diameter increases ideal speed; winning also depends on torque, slip, and the course.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
